res:traefik.description: Traefik v3 reverse proxy that reads Docker labels: it routes the main domain to the backend (port 8000) and adminer.<domain> to Adminer (port 8080). Locally it listens on port 80 and shows its dashboard on 8090.
res:traefik.purpose: Single public entry point in front of the containers.

res:postgres.description: PostgreSQL 18 container `db` with database `app` and two tables: `user` and `item`. Each item has an owner_id foreign key to user that is deleted with its owner; the schema is managed by Alembic migrations.
res:postgres.purpose: The only persistent store; the backend reaches it through SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with the psycopg driver.

svc:adminer.description: Adminer web UI for browsing and editing the PostgreSQL database, published by Traefik at adminer.<domain> and on port 8080 locally.
svc:adminer.purpose: Operator tool for inspecting tables by hand; the app itself never calls it.
svc:adminer.name: Adminer (database UI)

svc:mailpit.description: Mailpit fake SMTP server for local development: the backend sends mail to it on port 1025 (compose.override.yml sets SMTP_HOST to mailpit), and its web UI and API on port 8025 show every captured email.
svc:mailpit.purpose: Lets password-recovery and new-account emails be tested without a real mail provider; Playwright tests read reset links from it.
svc:mailpit.name: Mailpit (dev mail catcher)

unit:python:..description: Small Python helpers at the repo root: hooks/post_gen_project.py converts .sh files to LF line endings after a project is generated, scripts/prepare_release.py bumps the version and extracts release notes, and scripts/add_latest_release_date.py dates the newest release header.
unit:python:..purpose: Maintenance tooling used by the release workflows and pre-commit, not part of the running app.
unit:python:..name: Repo tooling scripts

unit:python:backend.description: FastAPI app (Python 3.14, SQLModel, pydantic-settings) with 23 endpoints under /api/v1 for login, password recovery, users, items and utils; it also serves the built frontend at /. Runs as compose service `backend` on port 8000, and scripts/prestart.sh runs Alembic migrations and creates the first superuser before it starts.
unit:python:backend.purpose: Holds all business rules and is the only part that talks to PostgreSQL, signs tokens and sends email.

unit:js:frontend.description: React 19 + TypeScript single-page app (Vite, TanStack Router and Query, Tailwind with shadcn/Radix UI) with login, signup, password recovery, dashboard, items, settings and admin pages. Vite builds it into backend/app/frontend and the backend serves it at /; the compose `playwright` service is only the end-to-end test runner.
unit:js:frontend.purpose: The user-facing UI; every action goes through the generated API client to /api/v1 on the backend.

unit:js:packages/react-email.description: React Email sources for the three transactional emails (new account, password reset, test email) plus shared layout pieces. `bun run email:export` renders them to HTML with Jinja placeholders into backend/app/email-templates.
unit:js:packages/react-email.purpose: Design-time source of the emails the backend sends; it is not deployed on its own.
unit:js:packages/react-email.name: Email templates (React Email)

dir:scripts.description: Release tooling: prepare_release.py bumps the version and updates release-notes.md (used by the prepare-release and create-draft-release workflows), and add_latest_release_date.py runs as a pre-commit hook.
dir:scripts.purpose: Automates the template's own release process.

dir:backend/app.description: The backend's Python package: main.py builds the FastAPI app, models.py defines the User and Item tables plus API schemas, crud.py has user and item database helpers, utils.py sends email and makes reset tokens, and initial_data.py seeds the first superuser.
dir:backend/app.purpose: Everything that runs inside the backend container.

dir:backend/app/alembic.description: Alembic migration environment: env.py points Alembic at SQLModel.metadata from app.models and at settings.DATABASE_URL.
dir:backend/app/alembic.purpose: Evolves the PostgreSQL schema; scripts/prestart.sh runs `alembic upgrade head` before the app starts.

dir:backend/app/alembic/versions.description: Migration scripts, starting with e2412789c190 which creates the `user` and `item` tables, followed by ones that switch ids to UUIDs, add string length limits, cascade deletes and created_at columns.
dir:backend/app/alembic/versions.purpose: The recorded history of the database schema.

dir:backend/app/api.description: HTTP layer: main.py mounts the login, users, utils and items routers (plus the private router only in development), and deps.py defines the shared dependencies SessionDep, CurrentUser and get_current_active_superuser.
dir:backend/app/api.purpose: Turns each request into an authenticated, database-backed handler call.

dir:backend/app/api/routes.description: One router per area: login.py (access token, password recovery and reset), users.py (signup, /users/me, admin user management), items.py (item CRUD scoped to the owner), utils.py (health check, test email) and private.py (dev-only user creation for end-to-end tests).

dir:backend/app/core.description: config.py loads settings from the environment and ../.env (secret key, DATABASE_URL, SMTP, first superuser) and rejects default secrets outside development; db.py creates the SQLAlchemy engine and init_db; security.py hashes passwords (Argon2 with bcrypt fallback) and signs JWTs.
dir:backend/app/core.purpose: Shared foundations every route depends on.

dir:backend/tests.description: Pytest suite that runs against a real PostgreSQL: conftest.py seeds the superuser, provides a TestClient and auth headers, and deletes all items and users at the end.
dir:backend/tests.purpose: Covers the API routes and CRUD helpers; CI fails below 90% coverage.

dir:backend/tests/api.description: API tests, grouped one module per router under routes/.
dir:backend/tests/api.purpose: Exercises the HTTP endpoints through FastAPI's TestClient.

dir:backend/tests/api/routes.description: test_login.py, test_users.py, test_items.py and test_private.py, one per router, including token login, password reset and the bcrypt-to-Argon2 hash upgrade on login.
dir:backend/tests/api/routes.purpose: Checks each endpoint's success and permission cases.

dir:backend/tests/crud.description: test_user.py: tests for the user helpers in crud.py, called directly against the database.
dir:backend/tests/crud.purpose: Checks user creation and authentication below the HTTP layer.

dir:backend/tests/utils.description: Test helpers that create random users and items and fetch auth headers (get_superuser_token_headers, authentication_token_from_email).
dir:backend/tests/utils.purpose: Shared setup for the backend tests.

dir:frontend/src.description: App source: main.tsx configures the API client (base URL from VITE_API_URL, token from localStorage) and sends the user back to /login on any 401 or 403; routes/ holds the pages, components/ the UI, client/ the generated API SDK and hooks/ shared logic.
dir:frontend/src.purpose: All code that ends up in the browser bundle.

dir:frontend/src/client.description: Generated by @hey-api/openapi-ts from the backend's openapi.json: sdk.gen.ts exposes LoginService, UsersService, ItemsService, UtilsService and PrivateService with one method per endpoint, and types.gen.ts holds the request and response types.
dir:frontend/src/client.purpose: The frontend's only way to call the backend; regenerate it with scripts/generate-client.sh instead of editing it.
dir:frontend/src/client.name: Generated API client

dir:frontend/src/client/client.description: Generated Axios wrapper that creates the axios instance, builds request URLs and attaches the auth token.
dir:frontend/src/client/client.purpose: Transport layer under the generated services.

dir:frontend/src/client/core.description: Generated helpers for auth headers, body, path and query serialization, and server-sent events.
dir:frontend/src/client/core.purpose: Low-level plumbing shared by the generated client.

dir:frontend/src/components.description: UI building blocks grouped by feature: Admin (user management dialogs), Items (item dialogs and table columns), UserSettings, Sidebar, Common (layouts, data table, error pages), Pending (loading skeletons) and ui (shadcn/Radix primitives).
dir:frontend/src/components.purpose: Everything the pages in routes/ are assembled from.

dir:frontend/src/components/Admin.description: Dialogs for superusers to add, edit and delete users (UsersService.createUser, updateUser, deleteUser), plus the column setup and row menu for the admin user table.
dir:frontend/src/components/Admin.purpose: The UI behind the Admin page.

dir:frontend/src/components/Common.description: Shared layout pieces: AuthLayout for the login and signup screens, DataTable, NotFound and error pages, Footer, Logo and the light/dark switch.

dir:frontend/src/components/Items.description: AddItem, EditItem and DeleteItem dialogs that call ItemsService and then refresh the `items` query, plus the item table columns and row action menu.
dir:frontend/src/components/Items.purpose: The UI behind the Items page.

dir:frontend/src/components/Pending.description: Skeleton placeholders shown while the items and users tables are loading.
dir:frontend/src/components/Pending.purpose: Loading states for the two data tables.

dir:frontend/src/components/Sidebar.description: App sidebar with Dashboard and Items links, an Admin link that appears only for superusers, and the current-user menu.

dir:frontend/src/components/UserSettings.description: Settings panels for editing your name and email (updateUserMe), changing your password (updatePasswordMe) and deleting your own account (deleteUserMe).
dir:frontend/src/components/UserSettings.purpose: The UI behind the Settings page.

dir:frontend/src/components/ui.description: 24 shadcn-style primitives built on Radix: button, dialog, form, input, table, sidebar, tabs, toast and more, including PasswordInput and LoadingButton.
dir:frontend/src/components/ui.purpose: The design-system layer every feature component uses.

dir:frontend/src/hooks.description: useAuth (current-user query, login, signup and logout, with the token kept in localStorage), useCustomToast, useCopyToClipboard and useIsMobile.
dir:frontend/src/hooks.purpose: Shared logic, mainly the client side of authentication.

dir:frontend/src/routes.description: TanStack Router file routes: public pages login, signup, recover-password and reset-password, and _layout.tsx, which guards every other page and redirects to /login when there is no token.
dir:frontend/src/routes.purpose: Defines the app's URLs and which ones need a login.

dir:frontend/src/routes/_layout.description: Signed-in pages: the dashboard (index), the items table, user settings, and admin, which loads the full user list for superusers.
dir:frontend/src/routes/_layout.purpose: The pages a user sees after logging in.

dir:frontend/tests.description: Playwright end-to-end tests: auth.setup.ts logs in as the first superuser and saves the session, then specs cover login, sign-up, password reset, items, admin and user settings.
dir:frontend/tests.purpose: Checks the whole stack through a real browser; CI runs them inside Docker Compose.

dir:frontend/tests/utils.description: Test helpers: mailpit.ts polls Mailpit's search API for emails, privateApi.ts creates users through the dev-only /private/users endpoint, plus random-data and login helpers.
dir:frontend/tests/utils.purpose: Lets end-to-end tests set up users and read emails.

dir:packages/react-email/emails.description: The three email templates, new_account, reset_password and test_email, whose default props are Jinja placeholders such as {{ project_name }} so the exported HTML can be filled in by the backend.

dir:packages/react-email/ui.description: Shared email building blocks: Layout, Heading, Button, Callout and Link.
dir:packages/react-email/ui.purpose: Keeps the three emails visually consistent.

res:sentry.description: Sentry error and performance tracking, initialised in backend/app/main.py only when SENTRY_DSN is set and FASTAPI_ENV is not development. The frontend does not report to Sentry.
res:sentry.purpose: Collects production exceptions and traces from the FastAPI backend.

res:jwt.description: PyJWT tokens signed with HS256 and the backend's SECRET_KEY: 8-day access tokens (core/security.py) and 48-hour password-reset tokens (utils.py).
res:jwt.purpose: Stateless login: the backend keeps no session table and just checks the token signature on every request.

res:fastapi_security.description: FastAPI's built-in OAuth2 password-flow helpers: OAuth2PasswordBearer reads the bearer token from each request (api/deps.py), and OAuth2PasswordRequestForm parses the email/password login form (routes/login.py).
res:fastapi_security.purpose: Gives every protected endpoint its token and the login endpoint its form; there is no external identity provider.

infra:ci.description: 15 GitHub Actions workflows: backend tests with a 90% coverage gate (test-backend.yml), Playwright end-to-end tests inside Docker Compose (playwright.yml), pre-commit and zizmor checks, release preparation, and two deploy paths: Docker Compose on your own server (deploy-docker-compose.yml) and FastAPI Cloud (deploy.yml).
infra:ci.purpose: Runs migrations through scripts/prestart.sh before tests and deploys, and keeps the repo checked, released and shipped.

actor:users.description: People using the web dashboard in a browser. Regular users manage their own items and profile; superusers also manage every account from the Admin page.
actor:users.purpose: Starting point of every request; they reach both the page and the API through Traefik.

actor:users->res:traefik.description: Browsers send every request, for the page and the API alike, to Traefik on port 80, which picks a container by host name.

actor:users->unit:js:frontend.description: People use the React dashboard in their browser; the page itself is downloaded from the backend through Traefik.

res:traefik->svc:adminer.description: Requests for adminer.<domain> are forwarded to Adminer on port 8080, based on its Docker labels.

res:traefik->unit:python:backend.description: Requests for the main domain go to the backend on port 8000: /api/v1/* reaches the API and every other path gets the built frontend.

svc:adminer->res:postgres.description: Compose starts Adminer after `db`; an operator logs into PostgreSQL through it to browse and edit tables.

unit:js:frontend->svc:mailpit.description: Only in tests: the Playwright container waits for Mailpit and reads password-reset emails from its API.

unit:js:frontend->unit:python:backend.description: Every screen calls /api/v1 through the generated Axios SDK with the access token as a bearer header: login, /users/me, item CRUD and admin user management.

unit:python:backend->res:fastapi_securit.description: OAuth2PasswordBearer pulls the bearer token out of each protected request, and the login route reads the email/password form.

unit:python:backend->res:jwt.description: On login the backend signs an HS256 access token; on every protected request get_current_user decodes and checks it. Password-reset links carry a separate signed token.

unit:python:backend->res:postgres.description: Each request opens a SQLModel session to read and write the user and item tables; at startup prestart.sh runs the Alembic migrations and seeds the first superuser.

unit:python:backend->res:sentry.description: When SENTRY_DSN is set outside development, uncaught exceptions and performance traces are sent to Sentry.

unit:python:backend->svc:mailpit.description: In local development the backend sends password-recovery, new-account and test emails over SMTP to Mailpit on port 1025.

add_edges.description: send_email delivers mail over SMTP to SMTP_HOST, which compose.override.yml sets to the mailpit service in development.

tours.title: What happens when you log in
tours.intro: Follow an email and password from the login form to a signed token and back.

stops.text: The login page checks the email format and an 8-character minimum password with zod, then hands the form to loginMutation from useAuth.
useAuth posts the form to /api/v1/login/access-token through the generated LoginService and saves the returned access_token in localStorage.
The backend route reads the OAuth2 password form and calls crud.authenticate. Wrong credentials get a 400 'Incorrect email or password', inactive accounts a 400 'Inactive user'.
authenticate looks the user up by email and verifies the password hash. If the email is unknown it still checks a dummy hash, so the response time does not reveal which emails exist.
The lookup reads the `user` table, where email is unique and indexed and only a hashed_password is stored, never the password itself.
create_access_token signs the user's id and an expiry with SECRET_KEY using HS256. By default the token is valid for 8 days.
On every later request get_current_user decodes the bearer token, loads that user from the database and rejects inactive users.

tours.title: How an item is created
tours.intro: From the Add Item dialog to a new row owned by the signed-in user.

stops.text: The Add Item dialog requires a title, allows an optional description, and calls ItemsService.createItem when submitted.
The generated SDK sends POST /api/v1/items/ through Axios. main.tsx configured the client to attach the stored access token to every call.
Before the handler runs, the CurrentUser dependency turns the token into a User; an invalid token stops the request with 403.
create_item copies the request body into an Item and sets owner_id to the current user, so nobody can create items for someone else.
The row lands in the `item` table: a UUID id, title, description, created_at, and owner_id pointing at user.id with ON DELETE CASCADE.
The dialog invalidates the `items` query, so the Items page fetches the list again. The backend returns only your own items unless you are a superuser.

tours.title: From a browser to PostgreSQL
tours.intro: The path every API request takes through the running containers.

quests.question: Where are passwords hashed?
quests.hint: crud.py and the users routes both import get_password_hash from the same place.
quests.explain: core/security.py builds a pwdlib PasswordHash with Argon2 first and bcrypt as a fallback. When someone logs in with an old bcrypt hash, verify_and_update returns a new Argon2 hash and crud.authenticate saves it.

quests.question: Which file issues the access token?
quests.hint: Start at the POST /login/access-token handler and follow the function it returns.
quests.explain: routes/login.py checks the credentials and calls security.create_access_token, which signs the user's id with SECRET_KEY (HS256) and an expiry of ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES.

quests.question: Where is the first superuser created?
quests.hint: Something runs right after the migrations, before the backend starts serving.
quests.explain: scripts/prestart.sh runs the migrations and then app/initial_data.py, which calls init_db. init_db creates the FIRST_SUPERUSER account from settings, with is_superuser set, if no user with that email exists yet.

quests.question: Which table stores items, and how does it know who owns them?
quests.hint: Look for the SQLModel class with table=True that has a foreign key.
quests.explain: Items live in the `item` table. owner_id is a foreign key to user.id with ON DELETE CASCADE, and items.py filters every non-superuser query by owner_id.

quests.question: Where does the backend decide who counts as an admin?
quests.hint: All admin-only routes share one dependency.
quests.explain: get_current_active_superuser in api/deps.py returns 403 unless user.is_superuser is true. Routes such as GET /users/ list it in their dependencies; the frontend's own checks (the Admin link, the admin page guard) only shape navigation.
